slice: Two worlds, one trade-off: in India and America alike, companies are trading payroll for AI chips and data centres.

callouts.text: GCC jobs cut in India this year, per EIIRTrend. 3AI puts it at 4,000–5,000.
30-year Treasury yield, the highest since 2004. The 10-year neared 5.15%.

stories.title: India’s GCCs: fewer seats, bigger say
points: Visa cut ~1,500, PayPal ~600; ServiceNow and others 100+.
India teams now share global cuts; retail and tech hit hardest.
stories.why: India now owns more AI and product decisions.

stories.title: Tata Sons reappoints Chandrasekaran
points: Five-year term passed by majority; Noel Tata voted no.
Trusts call the vote void; ex-SC judges back Tata Sons.
stories.why: Board vs. owner: who steers India’s largest group?

stories.title: RBI vets Bagchi for HDFC Bank’s top job
points: RBI sought views from IRDAI and ICICI’s Sandeep Bakhshi.
Deputy MD Kaizad Bharucha is reportedly the other name.
stories.why: Can an insurance chief return to run a mega-bank?

stories.title: What higher yields mean for your money
points: Fed hiked this month, its first since 2023; more signalled.
Record $6.53 diesel; some savings accounts now pay 4%+.
stories.why: Loans price off Treasuries; households feel it fast.

stories.title: AI is reading your online past
points: Screeners flag posts once 70% sure who wrote them.
Face matching can unmask pseudonymous accounts.
Some employers keep monitoring staff after hiring.
stories.why: Don’t over-scrub: thin footprints now raise flags too.

stories.title: California’s benefits for undocumented immigrants
points: Its authors argue state-funded programs extend benefits regardless of immigration status, putting the cost at more than $11 billion last fiscal year.
About 1.7 million people are enrolled in state-funded full-scope Medi-Cal for undocumented immigrants, at a cost near $10 billion a year.
They say a mixed-status family can qualify for public services such as CAPI cash aid, health cover and tax credits.
numbers: last fiscal year, per the authors
stories.why: California’s budget is under strain, and who qualifies for state-funded benefits is a live political fight. This is an opinion piece, so the figures are the authors’ framing.
